transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-07-28
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Diego Ramos (Redwood) — Lena Ortiz, Marcus Hale, Priya Singh (Sapphire Retail)

Summary:
Quick console walkthrough focusing on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown. Customer wants to understand token-level cost, per-route routing, and whether Dedicated/Private is required for PII-sensitive inference. Action: send pricing and security docs, schedule pilot benchmark.

Topics:
- Per-route dashboards and filters
- Token-level cost and allocation by route/model
- Batching/caching effects on unit economics
- Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs and SSO/KMS concerns
- Next steps: pricing, security pack, pilot benchmarks

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Uh this is Maya from Redwood, with Diego our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:05] Lena Ortiz: Good thanks. Excited to see the console walkthrough. We've been, um, looking at the per-route cost stuff in your docs and want to see it in action.
[00:12] Diego Ramos: Awesome. Quick note, I'll be sharing my screen — if you can't see it shout, sometimes the redwood controls label is transcribed as redwood control, sorry.
[00:20] Priya Singh: Screen visible.
[00:22] Marcus Hale: Yep.
[00:30] Diego Ramos: Cool. So, starting at the Console home, the usage analytics page gives you token-level breakdowns, per-route latency, and cost attribution. You can filter by model, route, date range, and customer tag.
[00:45] Marcus Hale: How granular is the cost allocation? Can we attribute cost down to a specific route and model combo?
[00:52] Diego Ramos: Yes, that's the idea. We do per-token compute accounting and also include infra amortization for Dedicated pools. So the dashboard shows cost per 1k tokens by route, and an aggregate cost center view. There's a toggle for amortized reserved costs vs on-demand.
[01:10] Lena Ortiz: And does that include batching/caching savings? Our ops team will want to see the delta if we enable prefix caching or bigger batch windows.
[01:18] Diego Ramos: Good question. We show a comparison mode — you can run a time-slice with batching on vs off, and the console models the expected token cost savings from KV cache hits and continuous batching. It's an estimate but based on the runtime metrics we collect.
[01:34] Priya Singh: I noticed a screenshot in the deck where certain routes are flagged as "high cost" — is that automated anomaly detection?
[01:41] Diego Ramos: There's a rules engine. We recommend setting a cost-per-response threshold per route; if it exceeds that for X days it flags and suggests actions like quantizing, model variant swap, or moving to a cheaper instance family.
[01:54] Maya Chen: To add, the Console also surfaces quality regressions if you hook up eval prompt sets, so you won't blindly down-quantize a route without seeing a potential quality impact.
[02:03] Lena Ortiz: That's helpful. From a compliance perspective, we need audit logs and per-request metadata retained for 12 months. Does Redwood support that in Hosted or only in Private?
[02:13] Diego Ramos: Hosted supports audit logs and retention tiers up to a certain limit; for strict 12-month retention with customer-controlled keying we'd recommend Dedicated or Private where KMS/HSM integration and long-term retention are standard. I'll attach the SOC 2 and retention doc.
[02:28] Marcus Hale: So Dedicated gives us both predictable throughput and customer-managed KMS?
[02:33] Diego Ramos: Correct — Dedicated pools can be placed in your VPC, and with Private you can go fully on-prem if required. There's sometimes confusion with the names — Dedicated = reserved capacity in our cloud with VPC peering; Private = customer-controlled deployment.
[02:47] Priya Singh: What's the latency delta if we go to a higher batching configuration to save costs? Our product requires sub-200ms for conversational routes.
[02:56] Diego Ramos: There's a tradeoff. For low-latency routes we recommend smaller batch windows and prefix caching, which keeps p99s low. Batching helps throughput and amortizes tokenizer overhead but increases tail latency if you wait too long. We surface latency SLO graphs per route so you can pick the sweet spot.
[03:14] Lena Ortiz: Can we set per-route policies to pin routes to low-latency nodes or fall back to cheaper models during traffic spikes?
[03:21] Diego Ramos: Yes — smart routing policies let you assign latency targets, cost budgets, and fallback model variants. The route config allows canary rollouts, A/B, and automatic fallback to a lower-cost model if the primary becomes unavailable.
[03:33] Marcus Hale: Cool. If we do a pilot, we'd want to run our top 10 routes and replicate traffic. How invasive is the instrumentation?
[03:40] Maya Chen: Minimal — you can route traffic to Redwood endpoints or use our proxy. For Dedicated and Private we provide a connector and a small agent that sends metrics to the Console. Marcus, Diego can follow up with the exact footprint.
[03:51] Marcus Hale: Perfect.
[03:54] Priya Singh: A couple of security questions: SSO/SAML support and role-based access? We need scoped access for PMs vs infra.
[04:01] Diego Ramos: Full SSO/SAML, SCIM for user provisioning, and RBAC in the Console. You can scope route visibility and who can change rollout policies. We also log all actions for audit.
[04:11] Lena Ortiz: Great. Any known limitations with HIPAA / PHI while doing inference? We process some order history that could be PII.
[04:19] Diego Ramos: We have customers in regulated spaces — Hosted can be okay with contract controls, but typically for PHI we recommend Private or a Dedicated pool with customer-managed keys and strict network controls. I'll send the compliance flyer.
[04:31] Marcus Hale: Back to cost — do you show effective costs after quantization? Like A100 fp16 vs a 4-bit quantized GA model?
[04:39] Diego Ramos: Yes, the Console supports model variant cost profiles — you can compare fp16, int8, and quantized 4-bit profiles and see estimated per-response savings and potential throughput differences. The Optimize tab recommends quantization per workload.
[04:53] Priya Singh: Is there an automated suggestion engine? You mentioned Optimize earlier.
[04:57] Maya Chen: Right — Optimize looks at traffic patterns, sequence length distribution, and suggests batching, caching, and model variants. It outputs expected cost savings and a confidence score.
[05:06] Lena Ortiz: I saw a screenshot with token-type breakdowns and 'hot prefixes' — is that identifying common user prompts that can be cached?
[05:13] Diego Ramos: Exactly. We highlight high-frequency prefixes and suggest putting them into prefix cache or templating them on the client. That can lead to big KV cache hit rates.
[05:22] Marcus Hale: Are developer-level logs linkable to trace IDs? We need to correlate latency spikes with infra metrics.
[05:28] Diego Ramos: Yes, each request has a trace ID; the Console integrates traces and you can export to your APM.
[05:34] Priya Singh: Any partners for on-prem deployments? We have to evaluate vendors.
[05:39] Maya Chen: We partner with a few systems integrators; for large Private deployments we often work with infra partners or your existing integrator.
[05:46] Marcus Hale: Objection — open question: why choose Redwood over Bedrock or OpenAI for our use case?
[05:51] Maya Chen: Great question. We position on serving and economics. If you care about predictable inference costs, per-route observability, and a consistent API across hosted/dedicated/private, Redwood is optimized for production economics and rollouts. Plus our Optimize tooling helps lower unit costs without sacrificing quality.
[06:10] Priya Singh: Let's talk pilot logistics — timeline and success criteria.
[06:14] Maya Chen: We typically run a 2-4 week pilot: ingest sample traffic for top routes, run benchmarks for latency and throughput, and compare cost estimates. Success: p99 latency under targets and 20-30% cost reduction vs current baseline for non-critical routes.
[06:28] Lena Ortiz: Sounds reasonable. We'll need to map who owns what inside Sapphire. Marcus to provide traffic profile, Priya to own product acceptance.
[06:35] Marcus Hale: Yep I'll export our top routes and send over.
[06:37] Diego Ramos: I'll also attach the console export with a sample per-route report and the reserved capacity amortization example.
[06:45] Priya Singh: Any rough pricing numbers you can share now?
[06:48] Maya Chen: I'll send the detailed worksheet after the call; high level: Hosted per-token with volume tiers, Dedicated monthly commit with lower per-token economics, and Private is pricing via enterprise licensing. We'll include example math for your traffic.
[06:59] Lena Ortiz: One more — do you support custom model variants? We might want to host our fine-tuned model.
[07:04] Diego Ramos: Yes, you can bring your own model; we support custom model onboarding in Dedicated and Private and in Hosted via curated BYO workflows. There are some constraints for kernel optimization but we can discuss.
[07:15] Priya Singh: Great.
[07:17] Maya Chen: Alright we'll recap. Next steps: Maya to send pricing and pilot template; Diego to send SOC2, KMS docs, and a sample per-route export; Marcus to share traffic profile and top 10 routes. We'll aim to schedule the pilot setup week of 2026-08-10.
[07:33] Marcus Hale: Sounds good. Thanks all.
[07:35] Lena Ortiz: Thanks everyone.
[07:36] Maya Chen: Thanks, bye.
